Subject: MAP, eval plan & sequencing questions for pilot onramp

Hi Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to formalize the mutual action plan (MAP) so our procurement and legal teams can plan the next 30 days. A few items we need clarity on from your side: 

- Recommended sequencing: should Silverline sign a DPA before MSA or do you prefer redlines on the MSA first?
- Expected turnaround on Redwood redlines (legal capacity)?
- Evidence and artifacts we need to collect for our security checklist (SOC2, data retention, logging examples).
- A simple acceptance timeline we can put in our internal workstream (evaluation -> pilot -> order form).

We’re aiming to start the pilot tech install the week of May 17, which means contract sign-off by May 7 to give legal and procurement enough runway. Can you confirm whether that schedule is feasible and who at Redwood we should expect to interact with from legal?

Attached: initial Silverline procurement checklist (for your reference).

Appreciate a short sync or a written MAP so we can share with our CFO and GC.

Best,
Jane Morris\Director, Strategic Procurement\Silverline Health

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jane Morris <jane.morris@silverlinehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com; vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP, eval plan & sequencing questions for pilot onramp

Jane —

Really helpful context, thanks. High-level answers in-line and a proposed 30-day MAP below. I’ll loop legal (Laura) to confirm exact DPA/MSA sequencing but the usual path we recommend is:

1) DPA execution or DPA-signing commitment (often signed earlier or at least agreed in redline) -> provides privacy guardrails so we can share scoped data for the pilot.
2) Parallel MSA redlines and commercial term review (covers liability, indemnities, SLOs).
3) Order form finalization (pricing/pilot seat count) and signature last.

Turnaround: our Legal team typically returns first-pass redlines within 3 business days for straightforward commercial edits; more complex indemnity/hosting edits can take 5-7 days. We’ll prioritize Silverline given the pilot timeline.

Proposed 30-day MAP (summary):
- Day 0 (Apr 23): Agree on sequencing and sign DPA commitment (email or DocuSign).
- Day 3-7: Redwood legal sends MSA redline (laura_bennett).
- Day 8-14: Commercial review and counter-redline from Silverline.
- Day 15-20: Finalize MSA and order form pricing.
- Day 21-30: Signatures + pilot scheduling (install week of May 17).

I’ve attached an editable MAP and a first-pass MSA (MSA_Silverline_v1.2.docx). Laura — can you confirm the DPA template we should send and whether we can start with a commitment signature (DocuSign) for the DPA, then iterate MSA redlines?

If that timeline looks OK to you, I’ll send a HubSpot task with the MAP and propose a 30-minute legal sync for next Monday.

Thanks,
Karthik\Senior Director, Strategic Accounts\Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Subject: Re: MAP, eval plan & sequencing questions for pilot onramp

Hi Jane / Karthik —

Thanks — quick legal note and proposed sequencing from Redwood Legal: we prefer a DPA in place (signed or at least execution-committed) before any production data flows. For the pilot we can accept a DocuSign "DPA commitment" (signature on the DPA template) which buys time for full MSA negotiation in parallel.

Required evidence for procurement/security:
- SOC 2 Type II report (most recent) — we can provide redacted attachments.
- Data retention & deletion policy excerpt (for pilot data).
- Audit logging examples (token-level or event logs description).

Sequencing we recommend:
1) DPA signed (DocuSign) by both parties — we can route the DPA template by EOD today.
2) MSA redline exchange within 3 business days (Laura to send first-pass).
3) Order form negotiation finishes once MSA commercial terms are agreed — order form signature after MSA.

I’ll attach the DPA template and a short checklist for evidence collection. We’ll mark items required for your GC vs. those operational items Silverline engineering can provide.

Attachments: DPA_Silverline_template.pdf; MAP-30d-checkpoints.xlsx

Let me know if you want legal on the call Monday; we can keep it to 20 minutes and focus on DPA scope and any non-standard liability asks.

Regards,
Laura Bennett\Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercial\Redwood Inference
